name: maestro
description: Multi-harness orchestration — plan a universe of demands into waves of concurrent Claude Code sessions and land them with one action. v1 design (rev2.1) at .claude/programs/maestro/design.md. Commands: /maestro:program-plan (BACKLOG demands → .claude/programs/<name>/plan.yaml, schema v2 — annotated canonically in common/plan-schema.yaml, shared with board-flow's single-track mode; maestro writes `mode: parallel-waves`, still reads v1 plans (waves only, no `mode`) so nothing on disk needs migrating, and /maestro:run refuses a single-track plan by naming the right path rather than erroring — gated by the invocable Definition-of-Ready common/bin/cepa-dor), /maestro:run (gc → intake → gatekeeper up → fork each slice into a herdr worktree with generated settings + normative wrapper → file-based event loop → merge train reusing worktree-merge guards → report; reads only plan.yaml), /maestro:resume (rebuild an interrupted wave from wave-state.yaml). Called with no program name, /maestro:run lists what this repo can actually run (mode, next pending wave, and why the ineligible ones are ineligible) via maestro-programs, instead of making the user guess a name. Deterministic cores in bin/ (tested): maestro-programs (read-only listing), maestro-fork-settings (camada 1 — deny-by-default + surface allow + ask-routes-to-gatekeeper), maestro-gatekeeper (permission mediation over shared loopback MCP HTTP, slice identity via query param, shadow-mode, escalation queue; proven as spike 2026-07-15), maestro-poll (event-loop iteration by file marker), maestro-wave-state (crash-recovery store, plus the `check-terminal` boundary: the wave does not reach the merge train or the report while any slice is still pending/running — those are the absence of a result, not a result, and a wave that lands with one makes that slice vanish unremarked; exit 2 names the offenders). End-to-end (herdr spawn + full wave) validated in construction step 4 — first real program. Requires common@cepa. NOVO em 0.5.0 — /maestro:program-plan --from-plan <nome>: a fonte passa a poder ser a fila single-track do repo (.claude/programs/<nome>/plan.yaml) em vez de um arquivo de prosa. E a promocao fila → ondas, ate aqui declarada MANUAL em docs/execution-plan.md por nao haver caminho, e a resposta a "como uso o program-plan num projeto com Jira": o --source so aceita arquivo, e a fila aceita o board como fonte (via /common:plan --from-jira). Quem le a fila e common/bin/cepa-plan promote, nao a prosa do comando — mesma licao das etapas 1 e 2, em que um paragrafo mandando "promova so os pending" so podia ser provado por um grep nele mesmo. O que a conversa acrescenta e o que a fila nao tem: superficie, aceite e gate humano. O `why` de cada item e COPIADO e nunca reescrito (e o criterio que colocou ele naquela posicao), o `onda_minima` que vem do `blocked_by` e PISO e nao sugestao (agrupar por superficie disjunta por cima dele faz a filha de baixo forkar antes de existir o que ela consome), e o plano de ondas precisa de um nome PROPRIO escolhido pelo dono — o --check-name da exit 3 no nome da fila, que e o mecanismo funcionando e nao um erro a contornar. Promover nao mexe na fila: os itens continuam `pending` la, e o risco que sobra (o mesmo item com dois executores possiveis, o /common:drain-plan e a onda) e dito em voz alta no encerramento. Regressao em tests/test_program_plan_from_plan.py, com os checkpoints `[from-plan:*]` medidos pelo cepa-promptcov.
